clue.text: Though out of key, the Spanish are superior

parts.note: the Latin prefix ex means out of or from
C is a musical key
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Spanish singers go off key yet still claim to be better than everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo others, being better than they are.

clue.text: Old soldier making his mark with a bow

definitions.text: making his mark with a bow

explanation.surface: A veteran fighter leaves his mark while taking a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowman was a soldier of old armies, and one who scores a hit on the target with a bow is also a bowman.

clue.text: The ordinary person among the very many weirdos

indicators.note: the letters sit among the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: An average citizen surrounded by a crowd of eccentrics.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'thE VERY MANy'; 'weirdos' just completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyman is the name used for a typical, average member of the public, from the medieval morality play.

indicators.note: the word ignored may be turned into a different word by rearranging it

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another clue that can safely be overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' is the answer to 15-across, used here as the definition: both words mean slowly wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Water gradually grinding rock away is said to be wearing it down, the same sense as eating it away.

explanation.surface: Something abandoned at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry the term means the left-hand side, and as a moral adjective it means low, wicked or evil.

parts.note: to rein is to control, as with a horse's reins
force means strength or vigour

explanation.surface: Back up your management with real energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen or prop up something is to bolster it, giving it support.

clue.text: Very green, but a good mixer

parts.note: extra used as an adverb means especially or very, as in extra careful
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: A newcomer who is very inexperienced yet socialises easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' suggests naivety, but here it is the heraldic colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, sociable person mixes happily in company; the variant spelling of extrovert.

clue.text: A man on horseback delivered the queen's letters

parts.note: rid as a past tense means freed or delivered, as in rid of a burden
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the queen

explanation.surface: A mounted messenger brings the monarch her post.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mounted on a horse is a horseman, one who sits and travels on it.

clue.text: Suspend for a quite mild imprecation

explanation.surface: Postponing things in favour of a gentle swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang something is to dangle it from above, and the exclamation 'hang it!' is a softened oath.

clue.text: Tied up by the heartless and the revolutionary

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word the is removed

parts.note: a red is a communist, a revolutionary

explanation.surface: Bound and gagged by a cold-hearted rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops H, the middle letter of the first 'the', leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal fastened by a rope to a post is bound or tied up.

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of a sling are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone untangles a sling that has got knotted.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring things into a straight line is to line them up or straighten them.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A flock gorging itself on grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself with food is to gorge or overeat.

indicators.note: a reading is an interpretation, so the name Antigone is interpreted as a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A performance of Sophocles' Antigone gets a poor reception.
explanation.walkthrough: Antigone is the heroine of a Greek tragedy, which makes 'reading' sound like a theatre reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal or denial is a thumbs-down, the gesture of rejection.

clue.text: A peer in the Tory party warning those who are behind

indicators.note: in means the peer is placed inside the political wing

parts.note: the Conservatives, or Tories, are the political right
an earl is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A nobleman in the Conservative party cautions the backbenchers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those who are behind' sounds like political backbenchers, but it means traffic following a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The red lamp at the back of a vehicle alerts following drivers to its presence.

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another clue that could prove tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' is the answer to 4-down, meaning eating away.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone slowly worn by water is being eroded, and a tedious or exhausting task is draining.

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
deemed means judged or considered

explanation.surface: Soldiers were thought to have been set free.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ransomed or bought back from captivity has been set free.

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray
a race is a people or tribe

explanation.surface: Nomadic clans in the desert battling for dominance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like sand; it is a verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: The fierce competitive struggle of modern working life to get ahead.

parts.note: 22-across means fools, so a pair of donkeys or idiots: ass twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bringing fools on board is an outrage!
explanation.walkthrough: '22' refers to the answer to 22-across, plural fools; two of them give ASS and ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A killer hired to murder someone is a criminal of the gravest kind.

parts.note: names a Victorian English composer of church music, whose surname also means one who colours or dyes things

explanation.surface: Asking who writes vividly coloured music.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John, the Victorian organist, wrote church music; a person who dyes or tints things is a colourer.

indicators.note: odd means the letters of red giant are put into a strange new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An astronomer notes a curious tilt in a red giant star.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope or incline is measured by how steeply it rises.

clue.text: Dines in a brasserie at seven o'clock

indicators.note: the letters run inside the words brasserie at seven

explanation.surface: Someone takes dinner at a French restaurant at seven.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a meal is to consume food, which is what one does when one dines.

explanation.surface: Pouring water off the pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain someone's energy is to weaken them, and noodle is old slang for a fool or simpleton.

parts.note: per means by or through, as in per post
taken as written
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Getting past is difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' suggests going past; here it means to die.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass away is to die.

explanation.surface: Taking back consent.
explanation.definitionFit: To go away from a place is to withdraw, and being allowed time off is authorisation or consent.

clue.text: Keeping a quarter in hand would be best

indicators.note: keeping means the closed hand holds the compass point within it

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand
NE, north-east, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Holding a coin in your palm would be the wisest course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' sounds like a coin; it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: The very best of something is its top quality, superlative of fine.

clue.text: One tenders change and it's popped in

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: change means the letters of tenders are altered into another order

explanation.surface: Someone offers coins and they are put in a slot machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put or placed into a slot has been placed inside it.

clue.text: Concerned with being among the few

indicators.note: among means the short word for concerning goes inside the article

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Belonging to an elite minority.
explanation.definitionFit: A small number, a handful, could be just a trio.

clue.text: Forgiving note followed by a letter

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a missive is a letter or written message

explanation.surface: A kind memo followed up by a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclined to pardon, giving remission of sins or debts.
